paper.title: Further Optimal Regret Bounds for Thompson Sampling

unmapped: Paper states model with rewards supported in [0,1]; analysis carried out for Bernoulli rewards, with extension to [0,1] via a cited reduction (AgrawalG12)
settings.definition_quote: We are given a slot machine with $N$ arms; at each time step $t=1, 2, 3, \ldots $, one of the $N$ arms must be chosen to be played. Each arm $i$, when played, yields a random real-valued reward according to some fixed (unknown) distribution with support in $[0,1]$. ... We provide the details of Thompson Sampling algorithm and our analysis for the Bernoulli bandit problem

bound.regime: 0 < epsilon <= 1; big-O treats mu_i, Delta_i as constants; only the additive N/epsilon^2 term is inside O

symbols.epsilon: free parameter of the analysis (not accuracy)

source.label: th:problem-dependent
source.quote: For the $N$-armed stochastic bandit problem, Thompson Sampling algorithm has expected regret $$\Ex[{\cal R}(T)] \leq (1+\epsilon) \sum_{i=2}^N \frac{\ln T}{d(\mu_i,\mu_1)} \Delta_i+ O(\frac{N}{\epsilon^2})  $$ in time $T$, where $d(\mu_i,\mu_1)=...$. The big-Oh notation in above assumes $\mu_i, \Delta_i, i=1, \ldots, N$ to be constants.

results.notes: N = K. The leading term has explicit constant (1+epsilon); only the additive term is O(N/epsilon^2) with hidden instance-dependent constants. Regret defined via expected pull counts (pseudo-regret).

source.label: th:problem-independent
source.quote: For the $N$-armed stochastic bandit problem, Thompson Sampling algorithm has expected regret $$\Ex[{\cal R}(T)] \leq O(\sqrt{NT\ln T})$$ in time $T$, where the big-Oh notation hides only the absolute constants.

results.notes: N = K. Algorithm does not use T.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic N-armed bandit, any (consistent) algorithm, problem-dependent asymptotic lower bound
